1.5: The sons of Yepheth: Gomer and Maḡoḡ, and Maḏai, and Yawan, and Tuḇal, and Mesheḵ, and Tiras.
1.6: And the sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, and Diphath, and Toḡarmah.
1.7: And the sons of Yawan: Elishah and Tarshishah, Kittim and Roḏanim.
1.8: The sons of Ḥam: Kush and Mitsrayim, Put and Kena’an.
1.9: And the sons of Kush: Seḇa, and Ḥawilah, and Saḇta, and Ra’mah, and Saḇteḵa. And the sons of Ra’mah: Sheḇa and Deḏan.
1.10: And Kush brought forth Nimroḏ; he began to be a mighty one on the earth.
1.11: And Mitsrayim brought forth the Luḏim, and the Anamim, and the Lehaḇim, and the Naphtuḥim,
1.12: and the Pathrusim, and the Kasluḥim from whom came the Pelishtites, and the Kaphtorim.
1.13: And Kena’an brought forth Tsiḏon, his first-born, and Ḥĕth,
1.14: and the Yeḇusite, and the Amorite, and the Girgashite,
1.15: and the Ḥiwwite, and the Arqite, and the Sinite,
1.16: and the Arwaḏite, and Tsemarite, and the Ḥamathite.
1.17: The sons of Shĕm: Ĕylam, and Ashshur, and Arpaḵshaḏ, and Luḏ, and Aram, and Uts, Ḥul, and Gether, and Mesheḵ.
1.18: And Arpaḵshaḏ brought forth Shelaḥ, and Shelaḥ brought forth Ĕḇer.
1.19: To Ĕḇer were born two sons: the name of one was Peleḡ, for in his days the earth was divided, and his brother’s name was Yoqtan.
1.20: And Yoqtan brought forth Almoḏaḏ, and Sheleph, and Ḥatsarmaweth, and Yeraḥ,
1.21: and Haḏoram, and Uzal, and Diqlah,
1.22: and Ĕyḇal, and Aḇima’ĕl, and Sheḇa,
1.23: and Ophir, and Ḥawilah, and Yoḇaḇ. All these were the sons of Yoqtan.
1.28: The sons of Aḇraham: Yitsḥaq and Yishma’ĕl.
1.29: These are their genealogies: The first-born of Yishma’ĕl was Neḇayoth, and Qĕḏar, and Aḏbe’ĕl, and Miḇsam,
1.30: Mishma, and Dumah, and Massa, Ḥaḏaḏ, and Tĕma,
1.31: Yetur, Naphish, and Qĕḏemah. These were the sons of Yishma’ĕl.
1.32: And the sons born to Qeturah, Aḇraham’s concubine: Zimran, and Yoqshan, and Meḏan, and Miḏyan, and Yishbaq, and Shuwaḥ. The sons of Yoqshan: Sheḇa and Deḏan.
1.33: And the sons of Miḏyan: Ĕphah, and Ĕpher, and Ḥanoḵ, and Aḇiḏa, and Elda’ah. All these were the children of Qeturah.
1.34: And Aḇraham brought forth Yitsḥaq. The sons of Yitsḥaq: Ĕsaw and Yisra’ĕl.
1.35: The sons of Ĕsaw: Eliphaz, Re’uw’ĕl, and Ye’ush, and Ya’lam, and Qoraḥ.
1.36: And the sons of Eliphaz: Tĕman, and Omar, Tsephi, and Gatam, and Qenaz, and Timna, and Amalĕq.
1.37: The sons of Re’uw’ĕl: Naḥath, Zeraḥ, Shammah, and Mizzah.
1.38: And the sons of Sĕ’ir: Lotan, and Shoḇal, and Tsiḇ’on, and Anah, and Dishon, and Ĕtser, and Dishan.
1.39: And the sons of Lotan: Ḥori and Homam; Lotan’s sister was Timna.
1.40: The sons of Shoḇal: Alyan, and Manaḥath, and Ĕyḇal, Shephi, and Onam. The sons of Tsiḇ’on: Ayah and Anah.
1.41: The son of Anah was Dishon. The sons of Dishon: Ḥamran, and Eshban, and Yithran, and Keran.
1.42: The sons of Ĕtser: Bilhan, and Za’awan, and Ya’aqan. The sons of Dishan: Uts and Aran.
1.43: And these were the melaḵim who reigned in the land of Eḏom before any meleḵ reigned over the children of Yisra’ĕl: Bela son of Be’or, and the name of his city was Dinhaḇah.
1.44: And when Bela died, Yoḇaḇ son of Zeraḥ of Botsrah reigned in his place.
1.45: And Yoḇaḇ died, and Ḥusham of the land of the Tĕmanites reigned in his place.
1.46: And when Ḥusham died, Haḏaḏ son of Beḏaḏ, who smote Miḏyan in the field of Mo’aḇ, reigned in his place. The name of his city was Awith.
1.47: And Haḏaḏ died, and Samlah of Masrĕqah reigned in his place.
1.48: And Samlah died, and Sha’ul of Reḥoḇoth ha’Nahar reigned in his place.
1.49: And Sha’ul died, and Ba’al-Ḥanan son of Aḵbor reigned in his place.
1.50: And Ba’al-Ḥanan died, and Haḏaḏ reigned in his place. And the name of his city was Pai. And his wife’s name was Mehĕtab’ĕl the daughter of Matrĕḏ, the daughter of Mĕy-Zahab.
1.51: And Haḏaḏ died. And the chiefs of Eḏom were Chief Timnah, Chief Alyah, Chief Yethĕth,
1.52: Chief Oholiḇamah, Chief Ĕlah, Chief Pinon,
1.53: Chief Qenaz, Chief Tĕman, Chief Miḇtsar,
1.54: Chief Maḡdi’ĕl, and Chief Iram. These were the chiefs of Eḏom.

10.1: And the Pelishtites fought against Yisra’ĕl. And the men of Yisra’ĕl fled from before the Pelishtites, and fell slain on Mount Gilboa.
10.2: And the Pelishtites pursued Sha’ul and his sons, and the Pelishtites smote Yahonathan, and Aḇinaḏaḇ, and Malkishua, sons of Sha’ul.
10.3: And the battle was heavy on Sha’ul. And the archers hit him, and he was wounded by the archers.
10.4: And Sha’ul said to his armor-bearer, “Draw your sword, and thrust me through with it, lest these uncircumcised ones come and abuse me.” But his armor-bearer would not, for he was much afraid, so Sha’ul took a sword and fell on it.
10.5: And when his armor-bearer saw that Sha’ul was dead, he also fell on his sword and died.
10.6: Thus Sha’ul and his three sons died, and all his house - they died together.
10.7: And when all the men of Yisra’ĕl who were in the valley saw that they had fled and that Sha’ul and his sons were dead, they forsook their cities and fled, and the Pelishtites came and dwelt in them.
10.8: And the next day it came to be, when the Pelishtites came to strip the slain, that they found Sha’ul and his sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.
10.9: And they stripped him and took his head and his armor, and sent word throughout the land of the Pelishtites to proclaim the news among their idols and among the people,
10.10: and put his armor in the house of their mighty ones, and fastened his head in the house of Daḡon.
10.11: And all Yaḇĕsh Gil’aḏ heard of all that the Pelishtites had done to Sha’ul,
10.12: and all the brave men arose and took the body of Sha’ul and the bodies of his sons. And they brought them to Yaḇĕsh, and buried their bones under the tamarisk tree at Yaḇĕsh, and fasted seven days.
10.13: Thus Sha’ul died for his trespass which he had trespassed against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, because he did not guard the Word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and also for asking a medium for to make inquiry,
10.14: and did not inquire of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. So He put him to death, and turned the reign over to Dawiḏ son of Yishai.

11.1: And all Yisra’ĕl came together to Dawiḏ at Ḥeḇron, saying, “See, we are your bone and your flesh.
11.2: “Also, in time past, even when Sha’ul was meleḵ, you were the one who led Yisra’ĕl out and brought them in. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim said to you, ‘Shepherd My people Yisra’ĕl, and be ruler over My people Yisra’ĕl.’ ”
11.3: So all the elders of Yisra’ĕl came to the meleḵ at Ḥeḇron, and Dawiḏ made a covenant with them at Ḥeḇron before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And they anointed Dawiḏ meleḵ over Yisra’ĕl, according to the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 by Shemu’ĕl.
11.4: And Dawiḏ and all Yisra’ĕl went to Yerushalayim, which is Yeḇus, where the Yeḇusites were, the inhabitants of the land.
11.5: And the inhabitants of Yeḇus said to Dawiḏ, “You do not come in here.” But Dawiḏ captured the stronghold of Tsiyon, the City of Dawiḏ.
11.6: And Dawiḏ said, “Whoever smites the Yeḇusites first becomes chief and commander.” And Yo’aḇ son of Tseruyah went up first, and became chief.
11.7: And Dawiḏ dwelt in the stronghold, so they called it the City of Dawiḏ.
11.8: And he built the city around it, from Millo round about, and Yo’aḇ restored the rest of the city.
11.9: And Dawiḏ went on and became great, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts was with him.
11.10: And these were the heads of the mighty men whom Dawiḏ had, who strengthened themselves with him in his malḵuth, with all Yisra’ĕl, to appoint him to reign over Yisra’ĕl, according to the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
11.11: And these are the number of the mighty men whom Dawiḏ had: Yashoḇ’am son of a Ḥaḵmonite, chief of the thirty. He had lifted up his spear against three hundred, slain at one time.
11.12: And after him was El’azar son of Doḏo, the Aḥoḥite, who was one of the three mighty men.
11.13: He was with Dawiḏ at Pasdammim, and the Pelishtites were gathered there for battle, and a portion of the field was filled with barley, and the people had fled before the Pelishtites.
11.14: But they took their stand in the midst of that field, and delivered it, and smote the Pelishtites. Thus 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 saved them by a great deliverance.
11.15: And three of the thirty chiefs went down to the rock to Dawiḏ, into the cave of Aḏullam, while the army of the Pelishtites encamped in the Valley of Repha’im.
11.16: And Dawiḏ was then in the stronghold, and the watch-post of the Pelishtites was then in Bĕyth Leḥem.
11.17: And Dawiḏ longed and said, “Oh, that someone would give me a drink of water from the well of Bĕyth Leḥem, which is by the gate!”
11.18: And the three broke through the camp of the Pelishtites, and drew water from the well of Bĕyth Leḥem that was by the gate, and took it and brought it to Dawiḏ. But Dawiḏ would not drink it, but poured it out to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
11.19: And he said, “Far be it from me, O my Elohim, that I should do this! Should I drink the blood of these men who have risked their lives? For at the risk of their lives they brought it.” And he would not drink it. This is what the three mighty men did.
11.20: And Aḇishai the brother of Yo’aḇ was chief of another three. And he had lifted up his spear against three hundred men, who were slain, and won a name among the three.
11.21: Of the three he was more esteemed than the other two men, so he became their head. However he did not come to the first three.
11.22: Benayah was the son of Yahoyaḏa, the son of a brave man from Qaḇtse’ĕl, who had done many deeds. He smote two lion-like Mo’aḇites. He also went down and smote a lion in the midst of a pit on a snowy day.
11.23: And he smote a Mitsrite, a man of great height, five ammah tall. And in the Mitsrite’s hand was a spear like a weaver’s beam, and he went down to him with a staff and wrenched the spear out of the Mitsrite’s hand, and slew him with his own spear.
11.24: This is what Benayahu Yahoyaḏa did, and won a name among the three mighty men.
11.25: See, he was more esteemed than the thirty, but he did not come to the first three. And Dawiḏ appointed him over his court.
11.26: And the mighty men of the armies were Asah’ĕl the brother of Yo’aḇ, Elḥanan son of Doḏo of Bĕyth Leḥem.
11.27: Shammoth the Harorite, Ḥelets the Pelonite,
11.28: Ira son of Iqqĕsh the Teqowite, Aḇi’ezer the Anathothite,
11.29: Sibbeḵai the Ḥushathite, Ilai the Aḥoḥite,
11.30: Maharai the Netophathite, Ḥĕleḏ son of Ba’anah the Netophathite,
11.31: Ithai son of Riḇai of Giḇ’ah, of the children of Binyamin, Benayah the Pirathonite,
11.32: Ḥurai of the wadis of Ga’ash, Aḇi’ĕl the Arbathite,
11.33: Azmaweth the Baḥarumite, Elyaḥba the Sha’albonite,
11.34: the sons of Hashĕm the Gizonite, Yahonathan son of Shaḡĕ the Hararite,
11.35: Aḥyam son of Saḵar the Hararite, Eliphal son of Ur,
11.36: Ḥĕpher the Mekĕrathite, Aḥiyahu the Pelonite,
11.37: Ḥetsro the Karmelite, Na’arai son of Ezbai,
11.38: Yo’ĕl the brother of Nathan, Miḇḥar son of Haḡri,
11.39: Tseleq the Ammonite, Naḥarai the Bĕrothite - the armor-bearer of Yo’aḇ son of Tseruyah,
11.40: Ira the Yithrite, Garĕḇ the Yithrite,
11.41: Uriyah the Ḥittite, Zaḇaḏ son of Aḥlai,
11.42: Aḏina son of Shiza the Re’uḇĕnite, the head of the Re’uḇĕnites, and thirty with him,
11.43: Ḥanan son of Ma’aḵah, and Yoshaphat the Mithnite,
11.44: Uzziya the Ashterathite, Shama and Ye’i’ĕl the sons of Ḥotham the Aro’ĕrite,
11.45: Yeḏiya’ĕl son of Shimri, and Yoḥa his brother, the Titsite,
11.46: Eli’ĕl the Maḥawite, and Yeriḇai and Yoshawyah the sons of Elna’am, Yithmah the Mo’aḇite,
11.47: Eli’ĕl, and Oḇĕḏ, and Ya’asi’ĕl of Metsoḇayah.

12.1: Now these are they who came to Dawiḏ at Tsiqlaḡ while he was still in hiding from Sha’ul son of Qish. And they were among the mighty men, helping the battle,
12.2: armed with bows, using both the right hand and the left, with stones, and with arrows, with bows, of the brothers of Sha’ul, of Binyamin.
12.3: The chief was Aḥi’ezer and Yo’ash, the sons of Shema’ah the Giḇ’athite; and Yezaw’ĕl and Pelet, the sons of Azmaweth; and Beraḵah, and Yahu the Anathothite;
12.4: and Yishmayah the Giḇ’onite, a mighty man among the thirty, and over the thirty; and Yirmeyahu, and Yaḥazi’ĕl, and Yoḥanan, and Yozaḇaḏ the Geḏĕrathite;
12.5: Eluzai, and Yerimoth, and Be’alyah, and Shemaryahu, and Shephatyahu the Ḥaruphite;
12.6: Elqanah, and Yishshiyahu, and Azar’ĕl, and Yow’ezer, and Yashoḇ’am the Qorḥites;
12.7: and Yo’ĕlah and Zeḇaḏyah, the sons of Yeroḥam of Geḏor.
12.8: And some Gaḏites separated themselves to Dawiḏ at the stronghold in the wilderness, mighty brave men, men trained for battle, who could handle shield and spear, whose faces were like the faces of lions, and were as swift as gazelles on the mountains:
12.9: Ĕzer the chief, Oḇaḏyah the second, Eliyaḇ the third,
12.10: Mishmannah the fourth, Yirmeyahu the fifth,
12.11: Attai the sixth, Eli’ĕl the seventh,
12.12: Yoḥanan the eighth, Elzaḇaḏ the ninth,
12.13: Yirmeyahu the tenth, Maḵbannai the eleventh.
12.14: These were from the sons of Gaḏ, chiefs of the army. The least was over a hundred, and the greatest was over a thousand.
12.15: These were the ones who passed over the Yardĕn in the first month, when it was overflowing all its banks, and put to flight all those in the valleys, to the east and to the west.
12.16: And some of the children of Binyamin and Yahuḏah came to Dawiḏ at the stronghold.
12.17: And Dawiḏ went out to face them, and answered and said to them, “If you have come peaceably to me to help me, my heart shall be united with you; but if to betray me to my enemies - there is no violence in my hands - let the Elohim of our fathers see and reprove.”
12.18: Then the Ruaḥ came upon Amasai, chief of the officers, “Yours, O Dawiḏ! And with you, O son of Yishai! Peace, peace to you, and peace to your helpers! For your Elohim shall help you.” And Dawiḏ received them, and put them among the chiefs of the raiding band.
12.19: And some from Menashsheh went over to Dawiḏ when he was going with the Pelishtites to battle against Sha’ul. But they did not help them, for the princes of the Pelishtites took advice and sent him away, saying, “He might go over to his master Sha’ul with our heads!”
12.20: When he went to Tsiqlaḡ, those of Menashsheh who went over to him were Aḏnah, and Yozaḇaḏ, and Yeḏiya’ĕl, and Miḵa’ĕl, and Yozaḇaḏ, and Elihu, and Tsillethai, chiefs of the thousands who were from Menashsheh.
12.21: And they helped Dawiḏ against the raiding bands, for they were all mighty brave men, and they were commanders in the army.
12.22: For at that time they came to Dawiḏ day by day to help him, until it was a great army, like an army of Elohim.
12.23: And these were the numbers of the chiefs of those that were armed for battle, and came to Dawiḏ at Ḥeḇron to turn over the malḵuth of Sha’ul to him, according to the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄:
12.24: Of the children of Yahuḏah bearing shield and spear, six thousand eight hundred armed for battle;
12.25: of the children of Shim’on, mighty brave men for the army, seven thousand one hundred;
12.26: of the children of Lĕwi four thousand six hundred;
12.27: and Yahoyaḏa, the leader of the Aharonites, and with him three thousand seven hundred;
12.28: and Tsaḏoq, a young man, a mighty brave man, and from his father’s house twenty-two commanders;
12.29: and the children of Binyamin, relatives of Sha’ul, three thousand - until then the greatest part of them guarded the charge of the house of Sha’ul;
12.30: and the children of Ephrayim twenty thousand eight hundred, mighty brave ones, men of name throughout their father’s house;
12.31: and the half-tribe of Menashsheh eighteen thousand, who were designated by name to come and appoint Dawiḏ to reign;
12.32: and the children of Yissasḵar who had understanding of the times, to know what Yisra’ĕl should do, their chiefs were two hundred. And all their brothers were at their command;
12.33: of Zeḇulun there were fifty thousand going out to the army, arranging battle with all weapons of battle, giving support with undivided heart;
12.34: and of Naphtali one thousand commanders, and with them thirty-seven thousand with shield and spear;
12.35: and of the Danites, arranging battle, twenty-eight thousand six hundred;
12.36: and of Ashĕr, going out to the army, arranging battle, forty thousand;
12.37: and of the Re’uḇĕnites and the Gaḏites and the half-tribe of Menashsheh, from beyond the Yardĕn, one hundred and twenty thousand armed for battle with every kind of weapon of battle.
12.38: All these men of battle, keeping rank, came to Ḥeḇron with a perfect heart, to appoint Dawiḏ to reign over all Yisra’ĕl. And all the rest of Yisra’ĕl were of one heart to appoint Dawiḏ to reign.
12.39: And they were there with Dawiḏ three days, eating and drinking, for their brothers had prepared for them.
12.40: And also those who were near to them, from as far away as Yissasḵar and Zeḇulun and Naphtali, were bringing food on donkeys and camels, on mules and cattle - food of flour and cakes of figs and cakes of raisins, wine and oil and cattle and sheep in great quantities, for there was joy in Yisra’ĕl.

13.1: And Dawiḏ consulted with the commanders of thousands and hundreds, and with every leader.
13.2: And Dawiḏ said to all the assembly of Yisra’ĕl, “If it seems good to you, and if it is of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim, let us send out to our brothers everywhere who are left in all the land of Yisra’ĕl, and with them to the kohenim and Lĕwites who are in their cities of their open lands, and let them be gathered to us;
13.3: and let us bring the ark of our Elohim back to us, for we sought Him not since the days of Sha’ul.”
13.4: And all the assembly agreed to do so, for the matter was right in the eyes of all the people.
13.5: So Dawiḏ assembled all Yisra’ĕl, from Shiḥor in Mitsrayim to as far as the entrance of Ḥamath, to bring the ark of Elohim from Qiryath Ye’arim.
13.6: And Dawiḏ and all Yisra’ĕl went up to Ba’alah, to Qiryath Ye’arim of Yahuḏah, to bring up from there the ark of Elohim, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, who dwells between the keruḇim, where the Name is called on.
13.7: And they placed the ark of Elohim on a new wagon from the house of Aḇinaḏaḇ, and Uzza and Aḥyo were leading the wagon.
13.8: And Dawiḏ and all Yisra’ĕl were playing before Elohim with all their might, and with songs, and with lyres, and with harps, and with tambourines, and with cymbals, and with trumpets.
13.9: And when they came to the threshing-floor of Kiḏon, Uzza put out his hand to hold the ark, for the oxen stumbled.
13.10: Then the wrath of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 burned against Uzza, and He smote him because he put his hand to the ark. And he died there before Elohim.
13.11: And Dawiḏ was displeased because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had broken out against Uzza, therefore that place is called Perets Uzza, until this day.
13.12: And Dawiḏ was afraid of Elohim that day, saying, “How shall I bring the ark of Elohim to me?”
13.13: So Dawiḏ did not take the ark with him into the City of Dawiḏ, but took it aside into the house of Oḇĕḏ-Eḏom the Gittite.
13.14: And the ark of Elohim remained with the household of Oḇĕḏ-Eḏom in his house three months. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 baraḵ the house of Oḇĕḏ-Eḏom and all that he had.

14.1: And Ḥiram meleḵ of Tsor sent messengers to Dawiḏ, and cedar trees, with stonemasons and carpenters, to build him a house.
14.2: And Dawiḏ knew that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had established him as meleḵ over Yisra’ĕl, for his malḵuth was highly exalted for the sake of His people Yisra’ĕl.
14.3: And Dawiḏ took more wives in Yerushalayim, and Dawiḏ brought forth more sons and daughters.
14.4: And these are the names of his children whom he had in Yerushalayim: Shammua and Shoḇaḇ, Nathan and Shelomoh,
14.5: and Yiḇḥar, and Elishua, and Elpelet,
14.6: and Noḡah, and Nepheḡ, and Yaphiya,
14.7: and Elishama, and Be’elyaḏa, and Eliphelet.
14.8: And when the Pelishtites heard that Dawiḏ had been anointed meleḵ over all Yisra’ĕl, all the Pelishtites went up to seek Dawiḏ. And Dawiḏ heard and went out against them.
14.9: And the Pelishtites came and made a raid on the Valley of Repha’im.
14.10: And Dawiḏ inquired of Elohim, saying, “Do I go up against the Pelishtites? And shall You give them into my hand?” And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to him, “Go up, and I shall give them into your hand.”
14.11: And they went up to Ba’al Peratsim, and Dawiḏ smote them there. Then Dawiḏ said, “Elohim has broken through my enemies by my hand like a breakthrough of water.” So they called the name of that place Ba’al Peratsim.
14.12: And they left their mighty ones there, so Dawiḏ commanded, and they were burned with fire.
14.13: And the Pelishtites once again made a raid on the valley.
14.14: And Dawiḏ again inquired of Elohim, and Elohim said to him, “Do not go up after them. Go around them, and come upon them in front of the mulberry trees.
14.15: “And it shall be, when you hear a sound of stepping in the tops of the mulberry trees, then go out to battle, for Elohim shall go out before you to smite the camp of the Pelishtites.”
14.16: And Dawiḏ did as Elohim commanded him, and they drove back the army of the Pelishtites from Giḇ’on as far as Gezer.
14.17: And the name of Dawiḏ went out into all lands, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 put the dread of him upon all nations.

15.1: And he built houses for himself in the City of Dawiḏ. And he prepared a place for the ark of Elohim, and pitched a tent for it.
15.2: Then Dawiḏ said, “No one is to lift the ark of Elohim but the Lĕwites, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has chosen them to lift the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and to serve Him forever.”
15.3: And Dawiḏ assembled all Yisra’ĕl at Yerushalayim, to bring up the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to its place, which he had prepared for it.
15.4: And Dawiḏ gathered the children of Aharon and the Lĕwites;
15.5: of the sons of Qehath: Uri’ĕl the chief, and one hundred and twenty of his brothers;
15.6: of the sons of Merari: Asayah the chief, and two hundred and twenty of his brothers;
15.7: of the sons of Gĕreshom: Yo’ĕl the chief, and one hundred and thirty of his brothers;
15.8: of the sons of Elitsaphan: Shemayah the chief, and two hundred of his brothers;
15.9: of the sons of Ḥeḇron: Eli’ĕl the chief, and eighty of his brothers;
15.10: of the sons of Uzzi’ĕl: Amminaḏaḇ the chief, and one hundred and twelve of his brothers.
15.11: And Dawiḏ called for Tsaḏoq and Eḇyathar the kohenim, and for the Lĕwites, for Uri’ĕl, Asayah, and Yo’ĕl, Shemayah, and Eli’ĕl, and Amminaḏaḇ,
15.12: and said to them, “You are the heads of the fathers of the Lĕwites. Qadosh yourselves, you and your brothers, then you shall bring up the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl to the place I have prepared for it.
15.13: “Because you did not do it the first time, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim broke out against us, because we did not ask Him about the Right-Ruling.”
15.14: So the kohenim and the Lĕwites qadosh themselves, to bring up the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl.
15.15: And the children of the Lĕwites bore the ark of Elohim on their shoulders, by its poles, as Mosheh had commanded according to the Word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
15.16: And Dawiḏ spoke to the leaders of the Lĕwites to appoint their brothers the singers with instruments of song, harps, and lyres, and cymbals, to lift up the voice with joy.
15.17: And the Lĕwites appointed Hĕman son of Yo’ĕl, and of his brothers, Asaph son of Bereḵyahu; and of their brothers, the sons of Merari, Ĕythan son of Qushayahu;
15.18: and with them their brothers of the second rank: Zeḵaryahu, Bĕn, and Ya’azi’ĕl, and Shemiramoth, and Yeḥi’ĕl, and Unni, Eliyaḇ, and Benayahu, and Ma’asĕyahu, and Mattithyahu, and Eliphelĕhu, and Miqnĕyahu, and Oḇĕḏ-Eḏom, and Ye’i’ĕl, the gatekeepers;
15.19: and the singers Hĕman, Asaph, and Ĕythan, were to sound the cymbals of bronze;
15.20: and Zeḵaryah, and Asi’ĕl, and Shemiramoth, and Yeḥi’ĕl, and Unni, and Eliyaḇ, and Ma’asĕyahu, and Benayahu, with harps besides sopranos;
15.21: and Mattithyahu, and Eliphelĕhu, and Miqnĕyahu, and Oḇĕḏ-Eḏom, and Ye’i’ĕl, and Azazyahu, to lead on the eight stringed lyres;
15.22: and Kenanyahu, leader of the Lĕwites, in the song, because he was skilled;
15.23: and Bereḵyah and Elqanah were doorkeepers for the ark;
15.24: and Sheḇanyahu, and Yoshaphat, and Nethan’ĕl, and Amasai, and Zeḵaryahu, and Benayahu, and Eli’ezer, the kohenim, were to blow the trumpets before the ark of Elohim. And Oḇĕḏ-Eḏom and Yeḥiyah, were doorkeepers for the ark.
15.25: And it was Dawiḏ and the elders of Yisra’ĕl, and the commanders over thousands, who went to bring up the ark of the Covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 from the house of Oḇĕḏ-Eḏom with joy.
15.26: And it came to be, when Elohim helped the Lĕwites who bore the ark of the Covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, that they offered seven bulls and seven rams.
15.27: And Dawiḏ was dressed in a robe of fine linen, as were all the Lĕwites who bore the ark, the singers, and Kenanyah the leader of the service with the singers. And Dawiḏ wore a linen shoulder garment.
15.28: So all Yisra’ĕl brought up the ark of the Covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 with shouting and with the sound of the horn, with trumpets and with cymbals, sounding with harps and lyres.
15.29: And it came to be, as the ark of the Covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came to the City of Dawiḏ, that Miḵal the daughter of Sha’ul, looking through a window, saw Meleḵ Dawiḏ dancing and playing. And she despised him in her heart.

16.1: And they brought the ark of Elohim, and put it in the midst of the Tent that Dawiḏ had pitched for it. And they brought burnt offerings and peace offerings before Elohim.
16.2: And when Dawiḏ had made an end of offering the burnt offerings and the peace offerings, he baraḵ the people in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
16.3: and gave a portion to everyone of Yisra’ĕl, both man and woman, to everyone a loaf of bread, a measure, and a cake of raisins.
16.4: And he appointed some of the Lĕwites to serve before the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, to bring to remembrance, and to thank, and to praise 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl:
16.5: Asaph the chief, and his second Zeḵaryah, Ye’i’ĕl, and Shemiramoth, and Yeḥi’ĕl, and Mattithyah, and Eliyaḇ, and Benayahu, and Oḇĕḏ-Eḏom, and Ye’i’ĕl, with harps and lyres, but Asaph was sounding with cymbals;
16.6: and Benayahu and Yaḥazi’ĕl the kohenim continually blew the trumpets before the ark of the Covenant of Elohim.
16.7: And on that day Dawiḏ first gave thanks to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 by the hand of Asaph and his brothers:
16.8:
Give thanks to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, call upon His Name, 
Make known His deeds among the peoples!
16.9:
Sing to Him, sing praise to Him, 
Speak of all His wonders!
16.10:
Boast in His qodesh Name, 
Let the hearts of those seeking 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 rejoice!
16.11:
Seek 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and His strength, 
Seek His face continually!
16.12:
Remember His wonders which He has done, 
His signs and the Right-Rulings of His mouth,
16.13:
O seed of Yisra’ĕl, His servant; 
O children of Ya’aqoḇ, His chosen ones!
16.14:
He is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim, 
His Right-Rulings are in all the earth.
16.15:
Remember His Covenant forever, 
The Word He commanded for a thousand generations,
16.16:
Which He made with Aḇraham, 
And His oath to Yitsḥaq,
16.17:
And He established it to Ya’aqoḇ for a Law, 
To Yisra’ĕl as an everlasting Covenant,
16.18:
Saying, “To you I give the land of Kena’an, 
The portion of your inheritance,”
16.19:
When you were but few in number, 
Few indeed, and sojourners in it.
16.20:
And they went up and down, 
From one nation to another, 
And from one reign to another people.
16.21:
He allowed no one to oppress them, 
And He reproved melaḵim for their sakes,
16.22:
“Do not touch My anointed ones, 
And do My neḇi’im no evil.”
16.23:
Sing to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, all the earth; 
Proclaim His deliverance from day to day.
16.24:
Declare His esteem among the nations, 
His wonders among all peoples.
16.25:
For great is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and greatly to be praised; 
And He is to be revered above all mighty ones.
16.26:
For all the mighty ones of the peoples are matters of naught, 
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 made the shamayim.
16.27:
Excellency and splendor are before Him, 
Strength and gladness are in His place.
16.28:
Ascribe to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, O clans of the peoples, 
Ascribe to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 esteem and strength.
16.30:
Tremble before Him, all the earth. 
The world also is firmly established, immovable.
16.31:
Let the shamayim rejoice, and let the earth be glad; 
And let them say among the nations, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall reign.”
16.32:
Let the sea roar, and all that fills it; 
Let the field rejoice, and all that is in it.
16.33:
Let the trees of the forest then sing before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
For He shall come to judge the earth.
16.34:
Give thanks to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, for He is good, 
For His kindness is everlasting!
16.35:
And say, “Save us, O Elohim of our deliverance; 
And gather us together, 
And deliver us from the gentiles, 
To give thanks to Your qodesh Name, 
And boast in Your praise.”
16.36:
Baruḵ be 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl 
From everlasting to everlasting! 
And all the people said, “Amĕn!” and praised 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
16.37: So he left Asaph and his brothers there before the ark of the Covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to perform regular service before the ark, as each day required;
16.38: also, Oḇĕḏ-Eḏom with his sixty-eight brothers, including Oḇĕḏ-Eḏom son of Yeḏuthun, and Ḥosah, to be gatekeepers;
16.39: and Tsaḏoq the kohĕn and his brothers the kohenim, before the Mishkan of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 at the high place that was at Giḇ’on,
16.40: to offer burnt offerings to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 on the altar of burnt offering regularly morning and evening, and to do according to all that is written in the Torah of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 which He commanded Yisra’ĕl;
16.41: and with them Hĕman and Yeḏuthun and the rest who were chosen, who were designated by name, to give thanks to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, because His kindness is everlasting;
16.42: and with them Hĕman and Yeḏuthun, to sound aloud with trumpets and cymbals and instruments for the songs of Elohim, and the sons of Yeḏuthun for the gate.
16.43: And all the people went, each one to his house, and Dawiḏ returned to baraḵ his house.

17.1: And it came to be, when Dawiḏ was dwelling in his house, that Dawiḏ said to Nathan the naḇi, “See, I am dwelling in a house of cedar, but the ark of the Covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is under curtains.”
17.2: And Nathan said to Dawiḏ, “Do all that is in your heart, for Elohim is with you.”
17.3: And it came to be that night that the word of Elohim came to Nathan, saying,
17.4: “Go, and you shall say to My servant Dawiḏ, ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “You do not build Me a House to dwell in.
17.5: “For I have not dwelt in a House since the time that I brought up Yisra’ĕl, even to this day, but have gone from Tent to Tent, and from Mishkan to another.
17.6: “Wherever I have moved about with all Yisra’ĕl, have I ever spoken a word to any of the rulers of Yisra’ĕl, whom I commanded to shepherd My people, saying, ‘Why have you not built Me a House of cedar?’ ” ’
17.7: “And now, say this to My servant Dawiḏ, ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, “I took you from the sheepfold, from following the sheep, to be ruler over My people Yisra’ĕl.
17.8: “And I have been with you wherever you have gone, and have cut off all your enemies from before you, and have made you a name like the name of the great men who are on the earth.
17.9: “And I shall prepare a place for My people Yisra’ĕl and plant them, and they shall dwell in a place of their own and move no more, nor shall the sons of wickedness oppress them anymore, as at the first,
17.10: since the time that I commanded rulers to be over My people Yisra’ĕl, and I have humbled all your enemies. And I declared to you that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 builds you a house.
17.11: “And it shall be, when your days are filled to go to be with your fathers, that I shall raise up your seed after you, who is of your sons. And I shall establish his malḵuth.
17.12: “He builds Me a House, and I shall establish his throne forever.
17.13: “I am to be his Father, and he is to be My son. And My kindness I do not turn away from him, as I took it from him who was before you.
17.14: “And I shall establish him in My house and in My Malḵuth forever, and let his throne be established forever.” ’ ”
17.15: According to all these words and according to all this vision, so did Nathan speak to Dawiḏ.
17.16: And Meleḵ Dawiḏ came in and sat before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and said, “Who am I, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim? And what is my house, that You have brought me this far?
17.17: “And this was a small matter in Your eyes, O Elohim, but You have spoken of Your servant’s house for a great while to come, and have looked upon me as though I were an exalted man, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim.
17.18: “What more could Dawiḏ add to You for the esteem of Your servant? For You know Your servant.
17.19: “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, for Your servant’s sake, and according to Your own heart, You have done all this greatness, in making known all these great matters.
17.20: “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, there is none like You, nor is there any Elohim besides You, according to all that we have heard with our ears.
17.21: “And who is like Your people Yisra’ĕl, the one nation on the earth whom Elohim went to redeem for Himself as a people; to make for Yourself a great and awesome Name, by driving out nations from before Your people whom You redeemed from Mitsrayim?
17.22: “For You appointed Your people Yisra’ĕl to be Your own people forever. And You, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, have become their Elohim.
17.23: “And now, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the word which You have spoken concerning Your servant and concerning his house, let it stand fast forever, and do as You have said.
17.24: “So let it stand fast, and Your Name be great forever, saying, ‘𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 of hosts, Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, is Elohim to Yisra’ĕl. And let the house of Your servant Dawiḏ be established before You.’
17.25: “For You, O my Elohim, have revealed to Your servant to build a house for him. Therefore Your servant has come to pray before You.
17.26: “And now, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, You are Elohim, and have promised this goodness to Your servant.
17.27: “And now, You have been pleased to baraḵ the house of Your servant to be before You forever. For You have baraḵ it, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and it is baruḵ forever.”

18.1: And after this it came to be that Dawiḏ smote the Pelishtites, and humbled them, and took Gath and its towns from the hand of the Pelishtites.
18.2: And he smote the Mo’aḇites, and the Mo’aḇites became Dawiḏ’s servants, and brought presents.
18.3: And Dawiḏ smote Haḏaḏezer meleḵ of Tsoḇah as far as Ḥamath, as he went to establish his power by the River Perath.
18.4: And Dawiḏ took from him one thousand chariots, and seven thousand horsemen, and twenty thousand foot soldiers. And Dawiḏ also hamstrung all the chariot horses, but left of them one hundred chariots.
18.5: And when Aram of Darmeseq came to help Haḏaḏezer meleḵ of Tsoḇah, Dawiḏ smote twenty-two thousand of Aram,
18.6: and Dawiḏ stationed men in Aram of Darmeseq, and the Arameans became Dawiḏ’s servants, and brought presents. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 saved Dawiḏ wherever he went.
18.7: And Dawiḏ took the shields of gold that were on the servants of Haḏaḏezer, and brought them to Yerushalayim.
18.8: And from Tiḇḥath and from Kun, cities of Haḏaḏezer, Dawiḏ brought a large amount of bronze, with which Shelomoh made the bronze sea, and the columns, and the vessels of bronze.
18.9: And when To’u meleḵ of Ḥamath heard that Dawiḏ had smitten all the army of Haḏaḏezer meleḵ of Tsoḇah,
18.10: he sent Haḏoram his son to Meleḵ Dawiḏ, to ask peace of him and baraḵ him, because he had fought against Haḏaḏezer and smote him - because Haḏaḏezer had been fighting against To’u - with all kinds of objects of gold, and silver, and bronze.
18.11: Meleḵ Dawiḏ also qadosh these to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, along with the silver and gold that he had brought from all these nations, from Eḏom, and from Mo’aḇ, and from the children of Ammon, and from the Pelishtites, and from Amalĕq.
18.12: And Aḇishai son of Tseruyah smote eighteen thousand Eḏomites in the Valley of Salt,
18.13: and he put watch-posts in Eḏom, and all the Eḏomites became Dawiḏ’s servants. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 saved Dawiḏ wherever he went.
18.14: So Dawiḏ reigned over all Yisra’ĕl, and he was doing right-ruling and righteousness to all his people.
18.15: And Yo’aḇ son of Tseruyah was over the army, and Yahoshaphat son of Aḥiluḏ was recorder,
18.16: and Tsaḏoq son of Aḥituḇ and Aḇimeleḵ son of Eḇyathar were the kohenim, and Shawsha was the scribe,
18.17: and Benayahu son of Yahoyaḏa was over the Kerĕthites and the Pelĕthites. And the sons of Dawiḏ were chiefs at the meleḵ’s side.

19.1: And after this it came to be that Naḥash the meleḵ of the children of Ammon died, and his son reigned in his place.
19.2: And Dawiḏ said, “Let me show kindness to Ḥanun son of Naḥash, because his father showed kindness to me.” So Dawiḏ sent messengers to comfort him concerning his father. And the servants of Dawiḏ came to Ḥanun in the land of the children of Ammon to comfort him.
19.3: And the chiefs of the children of Ammon said to Ḥanun, “Is Dawiḏ esteeming your father, in your eyes, because he has sent comforters to you? Have his servants not come to you to search and to overthrow and to spy out the land?”
19.4: So Ḥanun took Dawiḏ’s servants, and shaved them, and cut off their garments in the middle, at their buttocks, and sent them away.
19.5: And when some went and informed Dawiḏ about the men, he sent to meet them, because the men were greatly ashamed. And the meleḵ said, “Remain at Yeriḥo until your beards have grown, then return.”
19.6: And when the children of Ammon saw that they had made themselves a stench to Dawiḏ, Ḥanun and the children of Ammon sent a thousand kiḵars of silver to hire chariots and horsemen from Aram-Naharayim, and from Aram-Ma’aḵah, and from Tsoḇah.
19.7: So they hired for themselves thirty-two thousand chariots, with the meleḵ of Ma’aḵah and his people, who came and encamped before Mĕyḏeḇa. And the children of Ammon had gathered from their cities, and came to battle.
19.8: And when Dawiḏ heard, he sent Yo’aḇ and the entire army of the mighty men,
19.9: and the children of Ammon came out and put themselves in battle array before the gate of the city, and the melaḵim who had come were by themselves in the field.
19.10: And when Yo’aḇ saw that the battle had turned against him before and behind, he chose some of the choice ones of Yisra’ĕl, and put them in battle array to meet Aram.
19.11: And the rest of the people he put under the command of Aḇishai his brother, and they put themselves in battle array to meet the children of Ammon.
19.12: And he said, “If Aram is too strong for me, then you shall help me; but if the children of Ammon are too strong for you, then I shall help you.
19.13: “Be strong, and let us show strength for our people and for the cities of our Elohim, and let 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 do what is good in His eyes.”
19.14: And Yo’aḇ drew near, and the people with him, to battle against Aram, and they fled before him.
19.15: And when the children of Ammon saw that the Arameans were fleeing, they also fled before Aḇishai his brother, and went into the city. And Yo’aḇ came to Yerushalayim.
19.16: And when Aram saw that they had been smitten before Yisra’ĕl, they sent messengers and brought the Arameans who were beyond the River, and Shophaḵ the commander of Haḏaḏezer’s army went before them.
19.17: And it was reported to Dawiḏ, and he gathered all Yisra’ĕl, and passed over the Yardĕn and came upon them, and arranged in battle array against them. And Dawiḏ arranged in battle array against Aram, and they fought with him.
19.18: And Aram fled before Yisra’ĕl, and Dawiḏ slew seven thousand charioteers and forty thousand foot soldiers of the Arameans, and smote Shophaḵ the commander of the army.
19.19: And the servants of Haḏaḏezer saw that they were smitten by Yisra’ĕl, and they made peace with Dawiḏ and became his servants. And the Arameans would not help the children of Ammon any more.

2.1: These were the sons of Yisra’ĕl: Re’uḇĕn, Shim’on, Lĕwi and Yahuḏah, Yissasḵar and Zeḇulun,
2.2: Dan, Yosĕph and Binyamin, Naphtali, Gaḏ and Ashĕr.
2.3: The sons of Yahuḏah: Ĕr, and Onan, and Shĕlah, the three born to him by the daughter of Shuwa, the Kena’anitess. And Ĕr, the first-born of Yahuḏah, was evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and He slew him.
2.4: And Tamar, his daughter-in-law, bore him Perets and Zeraḥ. All the sons of Yahuḏah were five.
2.5: The sons of Perets: Ḥetsron and Ḥamul.
2.6: And the sons of Zeraḥ: Zimri, and Ĕythan, and Hĕman, and Kalkol, and Dara, five of them in all.
2.7: And the son of Karmi was Aḵar, the troubler of Yisra’ĕl, who trespassed in that which was under the ban.
2.8: And the son of Ĕythan was Azaryahu.
2.9: And the sons of Ḥetsron who were born to him: Yeraḥme’ĕl, and Ram, and Keluḇai.
2.10: Ram brought forth Amminaḏaḇ, and Amminaḏaḇ brought forth Naḥshon, leader of the children of Yahuḏah;
2.11: Naḥshon brought forth Salma, and Salma brought forth Bo’az;
2.12: Bo’az brought forth Oḇĕḏ, and Oḇĕḏ brought forth Yishai;
2.13: Yishai brought forth Eliyaḇ his first-born, and Aḇinaḏaḇ the second, and Shim’a the third,
2.14: Nethan’ĕl the fourth, Raddai the fifth,
2.15: Otsem the sixth, Dawiḏ the seventh.
2.16: And their sisters: Tseruyah and Aḇiḡayil. And the sons of Tseruyah: Aḇishai, and Yo’aḇ, and Asah’ĕl, three.
2.17: And Aḇiḡayil bore Amasa. And the father of Amasa was Yether the Yishma’ĕlite.
2.18: And Kalĕḇ son of Ḥetsron brought forth children by Azuḇah, his wife, and by Yeriyoth. Now these were her sons: Yĕsher, and Shoḇaḇ, and Ardon.
2.19: And Azuḇah died, and Kalĕḇ took Ephrath as his wife, who bore him Ḥur.
2.20: And Ḥur brought forth Uri, and Uri brought forth Betsal’ĕl.
2.21: And afterward Ḥetsron went in to the daughter of Maḵir the father of Gil’aḏ, whom he took when he was sixty years old. And she bore him Seḡuḇ.
2.22: And Seḡuḇ brought forth Ya’ir who had twenty-three cities in the land of Gil’aḏ.
2.23: And he took from them Geshur and Aram, with the towns of Ya’ir, with Qenath and its towns, sixty towns. All these were of the sons of Maḵir the father of Gil’aḏ.
2.24: And after the death of Ḥetsron in Kalĕḇ Ephrathah, Ḥetsron’s wife Aḇiyah bore him Ashḥur the father of Teqowa.
2.25: And the sons of Yeraḥme’ĕl the first-born of Ḥetsron were: Ram the first-born, and Bunah, and Oren, and Otsem, and Aḥiyahu.
2.26: And Yeraḥme’ĕl had another wife, whose name was Atarah; she was the mother of Onam.
2.27: And the sons of Ram, the first-born of Yeraḥme’ĕl, were Ma’ats, and Yamin, and Ĕqer.
2.28: And the sons of Onam were Shammai and Yaḏa. And the sons of Shammai: Naḏaḇ and Aḇishur.
2.29: And the name of the wife of Aḇishur was Aḇiḥayil, and she bore him Aḥban and Moliḏ.
2.30: And the sons of Naḏaḇ: Seleḏ and Appayim, and Seleḏ died without children.
2.31: And the son of Appayim was Yishi, and the son of Yishi was Shĕshan, and the son of Shĕshan was Aḥlai.
2.32: And the sons of Yaḏa, the brother of Shammai: Yether and Yahonathan, and Yether died without children.
2.33: And the sons of Yahonathan: Peleth and Zaza. These were the sons of Yeraḥme’ĕl.
2.34: And Shĕshan had no sons, only daughters. And Shĕshan had a Mitsrite servant whose name was Yarḥa.
2.35: And Shĕshan gave his daughter to Yarḥa his servant as wife, and she bore him Attai.
2.36: And Attai brought forth Nathan, and Nathan brought forth Zaḇaḏ,
2.37: and Zaḇaḏ brought forth Ephlal, and Ephlal brought forth Oḇĕḏ,
2.38: and Oḇĕḏ brought forth Yahu, and Yahu brought forth Azaryahu,
2.39: and Azaryahu brought forth Ḥelets, and Ḥelets brought forth El’asah,
2.40: and El’asah brought forth Sismai, and Sismai brought forth Shallum,
2.41: and Shallum brought forth Yeqamyah, and Yeqamyah brought forth Elishama.
2.42: And the sons of Kalĕḇ the brother of Yeraḥme’ĕl: Mĕysha his first-born, who was the father of Ziph, and the sons of Marĕshah the father of Ḥeḇron.
2.43: And the sons of Ḥeḇron: Qoraḥ, and Tappuaḥ, and Reqem, and Shema.
2.44: And Shema brought forth Raḥam the father of Yorqe’am, and Reqem brought forth Shammai.
2.45: And the son of Shammai was Ma’on, and Ma’on was the father of Bĕyth Tsur.
2.46: And Ĕphah, Kalĕḇ’s concubine, bore Ḥaran, and Motsa, and Gazĕz. And Ḥaran brought forth Gazĕz.
2.47: And the sons of Yahdai: Reḡem, and Yotham, and Gĕyshan, and Pelet, and Ĕphah, and Sha’aph.
2.48: Ma’aḵah, Kalĕḇ’s concubine, bore Sheḇer and Tirḥanah.
2.49: And she bore Sha’aph the father of Maḏmannah, Shewa the father of Maḵbĕna and the father of Giḇ’a. And the daughter of Kalĕḇ was Aḵsah.
2.50: These were the descendants of Kalĕḇ: The sons of Ḥur, the first-born of Ephrathah: Shoḇal the father of Qiryath Ye’arim,
2.51: Salma the father of Bĕyth Leḥem, Ḥarĕph the father of Bĕyth Gaḏer.
2.52: And Shoḇal the father of Qiryath Ye’arim had descendants: Haro’eh, half of the Menuḥothites.
2.53: And the clans of Qiryath Ye’arim: the Yithrites, and the Puthites, and the Shumathites, and the Mishraites. From these came the Tsor’athites and the Eshta’olites.
2.54: The sons of Salma: Bĕyth Leḥem, the Netophathites, Atroth Bĕyth Yo’aḇ, and half of the Menaḥtites, and the Tsor’ites.
2.55: And the clans of the scribes who dwelt at Yaḇĕts: the Tirathites, the Shim’athites, the Suḵathites. These were the Qĕynites who came from Ḥammath, the father of the house of Rĕḵaḇ.

20.1: And it came to be at the turn of the year, at the time melaḵim go out, that Yo’aḇ led out the forces of the army and destroyed the land of the children of Ammon, and came and besieged Rabbah. But Dawiḏ remained at Yerushalayim. And Yo’aḇ smote Rabbah and overthrew it.
20.2: And Dawiḏ took their meleḵ’s crown from his head, and found it weighed a kiḵar of gold, and there were precious stones in it. And it was put on Dawiḏ’s head. And he also brought out the spoil of the city, a very great amount.
20.3: And he brought out the people who were in it, and put them to work with saws, and with iron picks, and with axes. And thus Dawiḏ did to all the cities of the children of Ammon. Then Dawiḏ and all the people returned to Yerushalayim.
20.4: And afterward it came to be that fighting broke out at Gezer with the Pelishtites. Then Sibbeḵai the Ḥushathite smote Sippai of the sons of the giant, and they were humbled.
20.5: And there was fighting again with the Pelishtites, and Elḥanan son of Ya’ir smote Laḥmi the brother of Golyath the Gittite, the shaft of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam.
20.6: And there was fighting again at Gath, where there was a man of great size, with twenty-four fingers and toes, six and six. And he too was born to the giant.
20.7: And he reproached Yisra’ĕl, and Yahonathan son of Shim’a, Dawiḏ’s brother, smote him.
20.8: These were born to the giant in Gath, and they fell by the hand of Dawiḏ and by the hand of his servants.

21.1: And Satan stood up against Yisra’ĕl, and moved Dawiḏ to number Yisra’ĕl.
21.2: And Dawiḏ said to Yo’aḇ and to the rulers of the people, “Go, number Yisra’ĕl from Be’ĕrsheḇa to Dan, and bring the number of them to me so that I know it.”
21.3: And Yo’aḇ answered, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 adds to His people a hundred times more than they are. But, my master the meleḵ, are they not all my master’s servants? Why does my master seek to do this? Why should he be a cause of guilt in Yisra’ĕl?”
21.4: But the meleḵ’s word prevailed against Yo’aḇ. And Yo’aḇ left and went throughout all Yisra’ĕl and came to Yerushalayim.
21.5: And Yo’aḇ gave the sum of the number of the people to Dawiḏ. And all Yisra’ĕl had one million one hundred thousand men who drew the sword, and Yahuḏah had four hundred and seventy thousand men who drew the sword.
21.6: But he did not number Lĕwi and Binyamin among them, for the meleḵ’s word was loathsome to Yo’aḇ.
21.7: And it was evil in the eyes of Elohim, concerning this matter, and He smote Yisra’ĕl.
21.8: Then Dawiḏ said to Elohim, “I have sinned greatly, because I have done this matter. But now, I pray, take away the wickedness of Your servant, for I have done very foolishly.”
21.9: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Gaḏ, Dawiḏ’s seer, saying,
21.10: “Go, and you shall speak to Dawiḏ, saying, ‘Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “I hold three before you - choose one of them for yourself, and I do it to you.” ’ ”
21.11: So Gaḏ came to Dawiḏ and said to him, “Thus said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘Choose for yourself
21.12: either three years of scarcity of food, or three months to be defeated by your foes with the sword of your enemies overtaking you, or else for three days the sword of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, even the plague in the land, with the messenger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 destroying throughout all the borders of Yisra’ĕl.’ And now consider what answer I am to return to Him who sent me.”
21.13: And Dawiḏ said to Gaḏ, “I am in great trouble. Please let me fall into the hand of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, for His compassion is very great, but do not let me fall into the hand of man.”
21.14: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 sent a plague upon Yisra’ĕl, and seventy thousand men of Yisra’ĕl fell.
21.15: And Elohim sent a messenger to Yerushalayim to destroy it. And as he was destroying, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 saw, and relented about the evil, and said to the messenger who was destroying, “Enough! Now stop your hand.” And the messenger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was standing by the threshing-floor of Ornan the Yeḇusite.
21.16: And Dawiḏ lifted his eyes and saw the messenger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 standing between earth and the shamayim, having in his hand a drawn sword stretched out over Yerushalayim. And Dawiḏ and the elders, wrapped in sackcloth, fell on their faces.
21.17: And Dawiḏ said to Elohim, “Was it not I who commanded the people to be numbered? I am the one who has sinned and done evil indeed. But these, the sheep, what have they done? Let Your hand, I pray, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 my Elohim, be against me and my father’s house, but not against Your people, to be plagued.”
21.18: And the messenger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 commanded Gaḏ to say to Dawiḏ that Dawiḏ should go up to raise an altar to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 on the threshing-floor of Ornan the Yeḇusite.
21.19: So Dawiḏ went up at the word of Gaḏ, which he had spoken in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
21.20: And Ornan turned and saw the messenger. And his four sons with him hid themselves, and Ornan was threshing wheat.
21.21: And Dawiḏ came to Ornan, and Ornan looked and saw Dawiḏ, and he went out from the threshing-floor, and bowed down to Dawiḏ with his face to the ground.
21.22: And Dawiḏ said to Ornan, “Give me the site of the threshing-floor, so that I build an altar to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 on it. Give it to me at the complete price, so that the plague is restrained from the people.”
21.23: And Ornan said to Dawiḏ, “Take it for yourself, and let my master the meleḵ do what is good in his eyes. See, I shall give you the cattle for burnt offerings, the threshing implements for wood, and the wheat for the grain offering. I give it all.”
21.24: And Meleḵ Dawiḏ said to Ornan, “No, but I shall certainly buy it at the complete price, for I do not take what is yours for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, nor offer a burnt offering without cost.”
21.25: And Dawiḏ gave Ornan six hundred sheqels of gold by weight for the place.
21.26: And Dawiḏ built there an altar to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, and called on 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And He answered him from the shamayim by fire on the altar of burnt offering.
21.27: Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 commanded the messenger, and he returned his sword to its sheath.
21.28: At that time, when Dawiḏ saw that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had answered him on the threshing-floor of Ornan the Yeḇusite, he slaughtered there,
21.29: for the Mishkan of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and the altar of the burnt offering, which Mosheh had made in the wilderness, were at that time at the high place in Giḇ’on.
21.30: But Dawiḏ was unable to go before it to inquire of Elohim, for he was afraid of the sword of the messenger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.

22.1: Dawiḏ then said, “This is the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim, and this is the altar of burnt offering for Yisra’ĕl.”
22.2: And Dawiḏ commanded to gather the foreigners who were in the land of Yisra’ĕl. And he appointed stonemasons to cut hewn stones to build the House of Elohim.
22.3: And Dawiḏ prepared large quantities of iron for the nails of the doors of the gates and for the clamps, and more bronze than could be weighed,
22.4: and cedar trees beyond number, for the Tsiḏonians and those from Tsor brought much cedar wood to Dawiḏ.
22.5: And Dawiḏ said, “Shelomoh my son is young and tender, and the House that is to be built for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is to be exceedingly great, for a splendid Name, to all the lands. Please, let me make preparation for it.” So Dawiḏ made extensive preparations before his death.
22.6: He also called for his son Shelomoh, and commanded him to build a House for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl.
22.7: And Dawiḏ said to Shelomoh, “My son, as for me, it has been in my heart to build a House to the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 my Elohim,
22.8: but the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came to me, saying, ‘You have shed much blood and have fought great battles. You do not build a House for My Name, because you have shed much blood on the earth in My presence.
22.9: ‘See, a son is to be born to you, who is a man of rest. And I shall give him rest from all his enemies all around, for Shelomoh is his name, and peace and rest I give to Yisra’ĕl in his days.
22.10: ‘He builds a House for My Name, and he is to be My son, and I am to be his Father. And I shall establish the throne of his malḵuth over Yisra’ĕl forever.’
22.11: “Now, my son, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 be with you, then you shall prosper and build the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, as He has said to you.
22.12: “Only, let 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 give you wisdom and understanding, and command you concerning Yisra’ĕl, so that you guard the Torah of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim,
22.13: then you shall prosper, if you guard to do the Laws and Right-Rulings with which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 commanded Mosheh concerning Yisra’ĕl. Be strong and brave, do not fear nor be discouraged.
22.14: “See, in my affliction I have prepared for the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 one hundred thousand kiḵars of gold and one million kiḵars of silver, and bronze and iron beyond measure, for it is plenty. And I have prepared timber and stone, and you shall add to them.
22.15: “And with you there are many workmen: hewers and workers of stone and timber, and all types of skilled men for every kind of work.
22.16: “Of gold and silver and bronze and iron there is no limit. Rise up and do, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is with you.”
22.17: And Dawiḏ commanded all the rulers of Yisra’ĕl to help Shelomoh his son,
22.18: “Is not 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim with you? And has He not given you rest all around? For He has given the inhabitants of the land into my hand, and the land has been subdued before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and before His people.
22.19: “Now, give your heart and your being to seek 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim. And rise up and build the Miqdash of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim, to bring the ark of the Covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and the qodesh vessels of Elohim into the House that is to be built for the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”

23.1: And Dawiḏ was old and satisfied with days, and he made his son Shelomoh to reign over Yisra’ĕl,
23.2: and he gathered all the rulers of Yisra’ĕl, with the kohenim and the Lĕwites.
23.3: And the Lĕwites were numbered from the age of thirty years and above. And their number, head by head, was thirty-eight thousand males.
23.4: Of these, twenty-four thousand were to oversee the work of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and six thousand were officers and judges,
23.5: and four thousand were gatekeepers, and four thousand to give praise to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “which I made for giving praise.”
23.6: And Dawiḏ divided them into divisions, of the sons of Lĕwi: of Gĕreshon, Qehath, and Merari.
23.7: Of the Gĕreshonites: La’dan and Shim’i.
23.8: The sons of La’dan: Yeḥi’ĕl the head, then Zĕthan and Yo’ĕl, three.
23.9: The sons of Shim’i: Shelomith, and Ḥazi’ĕl, and Haran, three. These were the heads of the fathers’ houses of La’dan.
23.10: And the sons of Shim’i: Yaḥath, Zina, and Ye’ush, and Beri’ah. These were the four sons of Shim’i.
23.11: And Yaḥath was the head and Zizah the second. But Ye’ush and Beri’ah did not have many sons, so they were reckoned as one father’s house.
23.12: The sons of Qehath: Amram, Yitshar, Ḥeḇron, and Uzzi’ĕl, four.
23.13: The sons of Amram: Aharon and Mosheh. And Aharon was qadosh, he and his sons forever, that he should qadosh the most qodesh, to burn incense before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, to serve Him, and to baraḵ in His Name forever.
23.14: Now Mosheh, the man of Elohim, his sons were named after the tribe of Lĕwi.
23.15: The sons of Mosheh: Gĕreshom and Eli’ezer.
23.16: The sons of Gĕreshom: Sheḇu’ĕl was the head.
23.17: And the sons of Eli’ezer: Reḥaḇyah was the head. And Eli’ezer had no other sons, but the sons of Reḥaḇyah were very many.
23.18: The sons of Yitshar: Shelomith was the head.
23.19: The sons of Ḥeḇron: Yeriyahu was the head, Amaryah the second, Yaḥazi’ĕl the third, and Yeqam’am the fourth.
23.20: The sons of Uzzi’ĕl: Miḵah was the head and Yishshiyah the second.
23.21: The sons of Merari: Maḥli and Mushi. The sons of Maḥli: El’azar and Qish.
23.22: And El’azar died, and had no sons, but only daughters. And their brothers, the sons of Qish, took them.
23.23: The sons of Mushi: Maḥli, Ĕḏer, and Yerĕmoth, three.
23.24: These were the sons of Lĕwi by their fathers’ houses, the heads of the fathers’ houses as they were counted head by head by the number of their names, who did the work for the service of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, from the age of twenty years and above.
23.25: For Dawiḏ said, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl has given rest to His people, and He dwells in Yerushalayim forever,”
23.26: and also of the Lĕwites, “They shall no longer bear the Mishkan, or any of the vessels for its service.”
23.27: For by the last words of Dawiḏ the Lĕwites were numbered from twenty years old and above,
23.28: because their duty was to help the sons of Aharon in the service of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, in the courtyards and in the rooms, in the cleansing of all that was qodesh, and the work of the service of the House of Elohim,
23.29: both with the showbread and the fine flour for the grain offering, and with the unleavened cakes and what is baked on the griddle, and with what is mixed and with all kinds of measures and sizes;
23.30: and to stand every morning to thank and praise 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and so at evening;
23.31: and for all the burnt offerings to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 on the Shabbathoth and on the New Moons and on the Appointed Times, by number according to the Right-Ruling upon them, continually before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄;
23.32: and that they should guard the duty of the Tent of Appointment, the duty of the qodesh place, and the duty of the sons of Aharon their brothers in the service of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.

24.1: And the divisions of the sons of Aharon: The sons of Aharon were Naḏaḇ and Aḇihu, El’azar and Ithamar.
24.2: But Naḏaḇ and Aḇihu died before their father, and had no children, so El’azar and Ithamar served as kohenim.
24.3: And Dawiḏ, with Tsaḏoq of the sons of El’azar, and Aḥimeleḵ of the sons of Ithamar, divided them according to their offices in their service.
24.4: And there were more leaders found of the sons of El’azar than of the sons of Ithamar. So they divided the sons of El’azar into sixteen heads of their fathers’ houses, and the sons of Ithamar into eight heads of their fathers’ houses.
24.5: And they were divided by lot, one group as another, for there were officials of the qodesh place and officials of Elohim, from the sons of El’azar and from the sons of Ithamar.
24.6: And the scribe, Shemayah son of Nethan’ĕl, one of the Lĕwites, wrote them down before the meleḵ, and the rulers, and Tsaḏoq the kohĕn, and Aḥimeleḵ son of Eḇyathar, and the heads of the fathers’ houses of the kohenim and Lĕwites, one father’s house taken for El’azar and one for Ithamar.
24.7: And the first lot came forth to Yahoyariḇ, the second to Yeḏayah,
24.8: the third to Ḥarim, the fourth to Se’orim,
24.9: the fifth to Malkiyah, the sixth to Miyamin,
24.10: the seventh to Haqqots, the eighth to Aḇiyah,
24.11: the ninth to Yĕshua, the tenth to Sheḵanyah,
24.12: the eleventh to Elyashiḇ, the twelfth to Yaqim,
24.13: the thirteenth to Ḥuppah, fourteenth to Yesheḇ’aḇ,
24.14: the fifteenth to Bilgah, the sixteenth to Immĕr,
24.15: the seventeenth Ḥĕzir, to eighteenth to ha’Pitstsĕts,
24.16: the nineteenth to Pethaḥyah, the twentieth to Yeḥezqĕl,
24.17: the twenty-first to Yaḵin, the twenty-second to Gamul,
24.18: the twenty-third to Delayahu, the twenty-fourth to Ma’azyahu.
24.19: These were their offices in their service for coming into the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 according to their Right-Ruling by the hand of Aharon their father, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl had commanded him.
24.20: And the rest of the sons of Lĕwi: of the sons of Amram, Shuḇa’ĕl; of the sons of Shuḇa’ĕl, Yeḥdeyahu.
24.21: Concerning Reḥaḇyahu, of the sons of Reḥaḇyahu, the head was Yishshiyah.
24.22: Of the Yitsharites, Shelomoth; of the sons of Shelomoth, Yaḥath
24.23: and Bĕnai. Yeriyahu, Amaryahu the second, Yaḥazi’ĕl the third, and Yeqam’am the fourth.
24.24: Of the sons of Uzzi’ĕl, Miḵah; of the sons of Miḵah, Shamir.
24.25: The brother of Miḵah, Yishshiyah; of the sons of Yishshiyah, Zeḵaryahu.
24.26: The sons of Merari: Maḥli and Mushi; the son of Ya’aziyahu, Beno.
24.27: The sons of Merari by Ya’aziyahu: Beno, and Shoham, and Zakkur, and Iḇri.
24.28: Of Maḥli: El’azar, who had no sons.
24.29: Of Qish: the son of Qish, Yeraḥme’ĕl.
24.30: And the sons of Mushi: Maḥli, Ĕḏer, and Yerimoth. These were the sons of the Lĕwites according to their fathers’ houses.
24.31: These also cast lots, they too, as their brothers the sons of Aharon, in the presence of Meleḵ Dawiḏ, and Tsaḏoq, and Aḥimeleḵ, and the heads of the fathers’ houses of the kohenim and Lĕwites - the head of the fathers, as well as his younger brothers.

25.1: And Dawiḏ and the commanders of the army separated for the service some of the sons of Asaph, and of Hĕman, and of Yeḏuthun, who should naḇa with lyres, with harps, and with cymbals. And the number of the workmen according to their service was:
25.2: Of the sons of Asaph: Zakkur, and Yosĕph, and Nethanyah, and Ashar’ĕlah, the sons of Asaph at the hands of Asaph, who naḇu at the hands of the meleḵ.
25.3: Of Yeḏuthun, the son of Yeḏuthun: Geḏalyahu, and Tseri, and Yeshayahu, Ḥashaḇyahu, and Mattithyahu, six, under the hands of their father Yeḏuthun, who naḇu with a lyre to give thanks and to praise 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
25.4: Of Hĕman, the sons of Hĕman: Buqqiyahu, Mattanyahu, Uzzi’ĕl, Sheḇu’ĕl, and Yerimoth, Ḥananyah, Ḥanani, Eliyathah, Giddalti, and Romamti-Ezer, Yoshbeqashah, Mallothi, Hothir, Maḥaziyoth.
25.5: All these were the sons of Hĕman the meleḵ’s seer in the words of Elohim, to exalt his horn. For Elohim gave Hĕman fourteen sons and three daughters.
25.6: All these were at the hands of their father for song in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, with cymbals, harps and lyres, for the service of the House of Elohim: Asaph, Yeḏuthun, and Hĕman, at the hands of the meleḵ.
25.7: And the number of them, with their brothers who were taught in the songs of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, all who were skilled, was two hundred and eighty-eight.
25.8: And they cast lots for their duty, the small as well as the great, the teacher with the student.
25.9: And the first lot for Asaph came forth for Yosĕph; Geḏalyahu the second, he, and his brothers and sons, twelve;
25.10: the third Zakkur, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
25.11: the fourth Yitsri, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
25.12: the fifth Nethanyahu, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
25.13: the sixth Buqqiyahu, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
25.14: the seventh Yesar’ĕlah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
25.15: the eighth Yeshayahu, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
25.16: the ninth Mattanyahu, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
25.17: the tenth Shim’i, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
25.18: the eleventh Azar’ĕl, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
25.19: the twelfth Ḥashaḇyah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
25.20: the thirteenth Shuḇa’ĕl, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
25.21: the fourteenth Mattithyahu, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
25.22: the fifteenth Yerĕmoth, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
25.23: the sixteenth Ḥananyahu, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
25.24: the seventeenth Yoshbeqashah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
25.25: the eighteenth Ḥanani, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
25.26: the nineteenth Mallothi, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
25.27: the twentieth Eliyathah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
25.28: the twenty-first Hothir, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
25.29: the twenty-second Giddalti, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
25.30: the twenty-third Maḥaziyoth, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
25.31: the twenty-fourth Romamti-Ezer, his sons and his brothers, twelve.

26.1: For the divisions of the gatekeepers: Of the Qorḥites, Meshelemyahu son of Qorĕ, of the sons of Asaph.
26.2: And the sons of Meshelemyahu: Zeḵaryahu the first-born, Yeḏiya’ĕl the second, Zeḇaḏyahu the third, Yathni’ĕl the fourth,
26.3: Ĕylam the fifth, Yahoḥanan the sixth, Elyo’ĕynai the seventh.
26.4: And the sons of Oḇĕḏ-Eḏom: Shemayah the first-born, Yahozaḇaḏ the second, Yo’aḥ the third, Saḵar the fourth, Nethan’ĕl the fifth,
26.5: Ammi’ĕl the sixth, Yissasḵar the seventh, Pe’ullethai the eighth, for Elohim baraḵ him.
26.6: Also to Shemayah his son were sons born who ruled their fathers’ houses, because they were able mighty men.
26.7: The sons of Shemayah: Othni, and Repha’ĕl, and Oḇĕḏ, Elzaḇaḏ, whose brothers Elihu and Semaḵyahu were able men.
26.8: All these were of the sons of Oḇĕḏ-Eḏom, they and their sons and their brothers, able men with strength for the work: sixty-two of Oḇĕḏ-Eḏom.
26.9: And Meshelemyahu had sons and brothers, eighteen able men.
26.10: Also Ḥosah, of the children of Merari, had sons: Shimri the head - although he was not the first-born, his father made him the head,
26.11: Ḥilqiyahu the second, Teḇalyahu the third, Zeḵaryahu the fourth. All the sons and brothers of Ḥosah were thirteen.
26.12: These divisions of the gatekeepers, among the chief men, had duties like their brothers, to serve in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
26.13: And they cast lots for each gate, the small as well as the great, according to their father’s house.
26.14: And the lot to the east fell to Shelemyahu. Then they cast lots for his son Zeḵaryahu, a wise counsellor, and his lot came out to the north;
26.15: to Oḇĕḏ-Eḏom to the south, and to his sons the storehouse;
26.16: to Shuppim and Ḥosah to the west, with the Shalleḵeth Gate on the ascending highway; guard corresponding with guard.
26.17: On the east were six Lĕwites, on the north four each day, on the south four each day, and for the storehouse two by two.
26.18: As for the Parbar to the west, there were four on the highway and two at Parbar.
26.19: These were the divisions of the gatekeepers among the sons of Qoraḥ and among the sons of Merari.
26.20: And of the Lĕwites, Aḥiyahu was over the treasuries of the House of Elohim and over the treasuries of the qodesh gifts.
26.21: The sons of La’dan, the sons of the Gĕreshonites of La’dan, heads of their fathers’ houses, of La’dan the Gĕreshonites: Yeḥi’ĕli.
26.22: The sons of Yeḥi’ĕli, Zĕtham and Yo’ĕl his brother, were over treasuries of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
26.23: Of the Amramites, the Yitsharites, the Ḥeḇronites, and the Uzzi’ĕlites,
26.24: even Sheḇu’ĕl son of Gĕreshom, son of Mosheh, was overseer of the treasuries.
26.25: And his brothers by Eli’ezer were Reḥaḇyahu his son, and Yeshayahu his son, and Yoram his son, and Ziḵri his son, and Shelomoth his son.
26.26: This Shelomoth and his brothers were over all the treasuries of the qodesh gifts which Meleḵ Dawiḏ and the heads of fathers’ houses, the commanders over thousands and hundreds, and the commanders of the army, had qadosh.
26.27: Some of the booty won in battles they qadosh to maintain the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
26.28: And all that Shemu’ĕl the seer, and Sha’ul son of Qish, and Aḇnĕr son of Nĕr, and Yo’aḇ son of Tseruyah had qadosh, all who were under the hand of Shelomith and his brothers.
26.29: Of the Yitsharites, Kenanyahu and his sons were for the outward duties as officials and judges over Yisra’ĕl.
26.30: Of the Ḥeḇronites, Ḥashaḇyahu and his brothers, one thousand seven hundred able men, had the oversight of Yisra’ĕl beyond the Yardĕn westward, for all the work of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and in the service of the meleḵ.
26.31: Of the Ḥeḇronites, Yeriyah was head of the Ḥeḇronites according to his genealogy of the fathers. In the fortieth year of the reign of Dawiḏ they were sought, and there were found among them able men at Ya’zĕr of Gil’aḏ.
26.32: And his brothers were two thousand seven hundred able men, heads of fathers, whom Meleḵ Dawiḏ made officials over the Re’uḇĕnites, and the Gaḏites, and the half-tribe of Menashsheh, in all matters of Elohim and matters of the meleḵ.

27.1: And the children of Yisra’ĕl, according to their number, the heads of fathers, and the commanders of thousands and hundreds and their officers, served the meleḵ in all matters of the divisions which came in and went out month by month throughout all the months of the year, each division having twenty-four thousand.
27.2: Over the first division for the first month was Yashoḇ’am son of Zaḇdi’ĕl, and in his division were twenty-four thousand;
27.3: of the sons of Perets, and the chief of all the commanders of the army for the first month.
27.4: And over the division of the second month was Doḏai an Aḥoḥite, and of his division Miqloth also was the leader, and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
27.5: The third commander of the army for the third month was Benayahu, son of Yahoyaḏa the kohĕn, who was chief, and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
27.6: This was the Benayahu who was mighty among the thirty, and was over the thirty, and in his division was Ammizaḇaḏ his son.
27.7: The fourth for the fourth month was Asah’ĕl the brother of Yo’aḇ, and Zeḇaḏyah his son after him, and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
27.8: The fifth for the fifth month was Shamhuth the Yizraḥite, and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
27.9: The sixth for the sixth month was Ira son of Iqqĕsh the Teqowite, and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
27.10: The seventh for the seventh month was Ḥelets the Pelonite, of the children of Ephrayim, and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
27.11: The eighth for the eighth month was Sibbeḵai the Ḥushathite, of the Zarḥites, and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
27.12: The ninth for the ninth month was Aḇi’ezer the Anathothite, of the Binyamites, and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
27.13: The tenth for the tenth month was Maharai the Netophathite, of the Zarḥites, and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
27.14: The eleventh for the eleventh month was Benayah the Pirathonite, of the children of Ephrayim, and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
27.15: The twelfth for the twelfth month was Ḥeldai the Netophathite, of Othni’ĕl, and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
27.16: And over the tribes of Yisra’ĕl: the chief officer over Re’uḇĕn: Eli’ezer son of Ziḵri; over Shim’on: Shephatyahu son of Ma’aḵah;
27.17: Lĕwi: Ḥashaḇyah son of Qemu’ĕl; over Aharon: Tsaḏoq;
27.18: Yahuḏah: Elihu, one of Dawiḏ’s brothers; Yissasḵar: Omri son of Miḵa’ĕl;
27.19: Zeḇulun: Yishmayahu son of Oḇaḏyahu; Naphtali: Yerimoth son of Azri’ĕl;
27.20: the children of Ephrayim: Hoshĕa son of Azazyahu; the half-tribe of Menashsheh: Yo’ĕl son of Peḏayahu;
27.21: the half-tribe of Menashsheh in Gil’aḏ: Iddo son of Zeḵaryahu; Binyamin: Ya’asi’ĕl son of Aḇnĕr;
27.22: Dan: Azar’ĕl son of Yeroḥam. These were the rulers of the tribes of Yisra’ĕl.
27.23: But Dawiḏ did not take the number of those twenty years old and under, because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had said He would increase Yisra’ĕl like the stars of the shamayim.
27.24: Yo’aḇ son of Tseruyah began a census, but he did not finish, for wrath came upon Yisra’ĕl because of this census; nor was the number recorded in the account of the annals of Meleḵ Dawiḏ.
27.25: And Azmaweth son of Aḏi’ĕl was over the meleḵ’s treasuries. And Yahonathan son of Uzziyahu was over the storehouses in the field, in the cities, and in the villages, and in the watchtowers.
27.26: And Ezri son of Keluḇ was over those who did the work of the field for tilling the ground.
27.27: And Shim’i the Ramalhite was over the vineyards, and Zaḇdi the Shiphmite was over the increase of the vineyards for the wine cellars.
27.28: And Ba’al-Ḥanan the Geḏĕrite was over the olive trees and the sycamore trees that were in the low country, and Yo’ash was over the oil-stores.
27.29: And Shitrai the Sharonite was over the herds that fed in Sharon, and Shaphat son of Aḏlai was over the herds that were in the valleys.
27.30: And Oḇil the Yishma’ĕlite was over the camels, and Yeḥdeyahu the Mĕronothite was over the donkeys,
27.31: and Yaziz the Haḡrite was over the flocks. All of these were heads over the property of Meleḵ Dawiḏ.
27.32: Also Yahonathan, Dawiḏ’s uncle, was a counsellor, a wise man and a scribe. And Yeḥi’ĕl son of Ḥaḵmoni was with the meleḵ’s sons.
27.33: And Aḥithophel was the meleḵ’s counsellor, and Ḥushai the Arkite was the meleḵ’s companion.
27.34: And after Aḥithophel was Yahoyaḏa son of Benayahu, then Eḇyathar. And the chief of the meleḵ’s army was Yo’aḇ.

28.1: And Dawiḏ assembled at Yerushalayim all the rulers of Yisra’ĕl: the rulers of the tribes and the commanders of the divisions who served the meleḵ, the commanders over thousands and commanders over hundreds, and the heads over all the property and possessions of the meleḵ and of his sons, with the officials, the mighty men, and all the mighty brave men.
28.2: Then Meleḵ Dawiḏ rose to his feet and said, “Hear me, my brothers and my people: I had it in my heart to build a House of rest for the ark of the Covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and for the footstool of our Elohim, and had made preparations to build it.
28.3: “But Elohim said to me, ‘You do not build a House for My Name, because you have been a man of battle and have shed blood.’
28.4: “Yet 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl chose me above all the house of my father to be meleḵ over Yisra’ĕl forever, for He has chosen Yahuḏah to be the ruler. And of the house of Yahuḏah, the house of my father, and among the sons of my father, He was pleased with me to make me reign over all Yisra’ĕl.
28.5: “And of all my sons - for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has given me many sons - He has chosen my son Shelomoh to sit on the throne of the Malḵuth of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 over Yisra’ĕl,
28.6: and said to me, ‘Shelomoh your son is the one to build My house and My courtyards, for I have chosen him to be My son, and I Myself am a Father to him.
28.7: ‘And I shall establish his malḵuth forever, if he is strong to do My Commands and My Right-Rulings, as it is this day.’
28.8: “And now, before the eyes of all Yisra’ĕl, the assembly of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and in the hearing of our Elohim, guard and seek all the Commands of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, so that you possess this good land, and leave it as an inheritance for your children after you forever.
28.9: “As for you, my son Shelomoh, know the Elohim of your father, and serve Him with a perfect heart and with a pleasing life, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 searches all hearts and understands all the intent of the thoughts. If you do seek Him, He is found by you; but if you forsake Him, He rejects you forever.
28.10: “See, now, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has chosen you to build a House for the Miqdash. Be strong, and do it.”
28.11: And Dawiḏ gave his son Shelomoh the plans for the porch, and its houses, and its treasuries, and its upper rooms, and its inner rooms, and the place of atonement;
28.12: and the plans for all that he had by the Ruaḥ, of the courtyards of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and of all the rooms all around, and of the treasuries of the House of Elohim, and of the treasuries for the qodesh gifts;
28.13: and for the divisions of the kohenim and the Lĕwites, and for all the work of the service of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and for all the vessels of service in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄;
28.14: even gold by weight for utensils of gold, for all used in every kind of service; for silver for all utensils of silver by weight, for all utensils used in every kind of service;
28.15: and by weight for the lampstands of gold, and their lamps of gold, by weight for each lampstand and its lamps; and for the lampstands of silver by weight, for the lampstand and its lamps, according to the use of each lampstand;
28.16: and by weight, gold for the tables of the showbread, for each table, and silver for the tables of silver;
28.17: and clean gold for the forks, and the basins, and the jars of clean gold, and the golden bowls, by weight for every bowl; and for the silver bowls, silver by weight for every bowl;
28.18: and refined gold by weight for the altar of incense, and for the pattern of the chariot of the gold keruḇim, spreading out their wings and covering over the ark of the Covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
28.19: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 made me understand all this in writing, by His hand upon me, all the works of these plans.”
28.20: And Dawiḏ said his son Shelomoh, “Be strong and courageous, and do it. Do not fear nor be afraid, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim, my Elohim, is with you. He shall not leave you nor forsake you, until you have completed all the work for the service of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
28.21: “And see, the divisions of the kohenim and the Lĕwites for all the service of the House of Elohim, and every volunteer of any skill is with you in all work, for every kind of service. And the rulers and all the people are entirely at your command.”

29.1: And Dawiḏ the meleḵ said to all the assembly, “My son Shelomoh, the one whom Elohim has chosen, is young and tender. And the work is great, because the Palace is not for man but for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim.
29.2: “And with all my power I have prepared for the House of my Elohim: the gold for the gold, and the silver for the silver, and the bronze for the bronze, the iron for the iron, and the wood for the wood, shoham stones, and mountings, and colored stones of various colors, and all kinds of precious stones, and marble slabs - in large quantities.
29.3: “And also, because I delighted in the House of my Elohim, I have treasure of gold and silver; I give for the House of my Elohim even more than all that I have prepared for the Qodesh House:
29.4: three thousand kiḵars of gold, of the gold of Ophir, and seven thousand kiḵars of refined silver, to overlay the walls of the houses;
29.5: the gold for the gold and the silver for the silver, and for all kinds of work to be done by the hands of craftsmen. Who then is moved to fill his hand today for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄?”
29.6: And the leaders of the fathers, and the leaders of the tribes of Yisra’ĕl, and the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, with the heads over the meleḵ’s work, volunteered
29.7: and gave for the work of the House of Elohim five thousand kiḵars and ten thousand darics of gold, and ten thousand kiḵars of silver, and eighteen thousand kiḵars of bronze, and one hundred thousand kiḵars of iron.
29.8: And those with whom were found stones gave them to the treasury of the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, into the hand of Yeḥi’ĕl the Gĕreshonite.
29.9: And the people rejoiced, for they had given voluntarily, because with a perfect heart they had given voluntarily to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And Dawiḏ the meleḵ also rejoiced greatly.
29.10: And Dawiḏ baraḵ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 before all the assembly. And Dawiḏ said, “Baruḵ are You, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, our Father, forever and ever.
29.11: “Yours, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, is the greatness, the power and the comeliness, the pre-eminence and the excellency, because of all that is in the shamayim and in the earth. Yours is the reign, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and You are exalted as head above all.
29.12: “And the riches and the esteem come from Your presence, and You rule over all. And in Your hand is power and might, and in Your hand to make great and to give strength to all.
29.13: “And now, our Elohim, we thank You and praise Your splendid Name.
29.14: “But who am I, and who are my people, that we should be able to give so voluntarily as this? For all comes from You, and we have given to You out of Your hand.
29.15: “For we are sojourners and pilgrims before You, as were all our fathers; our days on earth are as a shadow, and without permanence.
29.16: “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim, all this store that we have prepared to build You a House for Your qodesh Name is from Your hand, and all is of You.
29.17: “And I know, my Elohim, that You are trying the heart and desire uprightness. As for me, in the uprightness of my heart I have voluntarily given all these. And now with joy I have seen Your people, who are present here to give voluntarily to You.
